standing.title: Smorgasburg Prospect Park
standing.address: Breeze Hill, Prospect Park (enter at Lincoln Road), Brooklyn, NY
standing.description: Brooklyn's open-air food market at Breeze Hill in Prospect Park, with dozens of independent vendors. Free to enter; pay per stall.
standing.time_note: Sundays 11am-6pm; arrive before noon to beat the line.
standing.practical_note: Entirely outdoors; check the forecast and bring water in heat.
standing.date_idea_reason: Open-air food market you can graze through together, then walk into Prospect Park.
standing.why_now: Runs every Sunday of the season and pairs naturally with a Prospect Park afternoon.

standing.title: NYC Resistor Public Craft Night
standing.description: Open craft night at the NYC Resistor hacker collective: bring a project, use the space, meet members. Free and open to the public, 18 and over.
standing.time_note: Mondays and Thursdays 6:30-9:30pm. Free, but 18+ only.
standing.practical_note: Fourth-floor walkup; confirm on Eventbrite since craft night is occasionally cancelled for private classes.
standing.date_idea_reason: A free, hands-on makerspace evening is an unusual low-cost date with something to actually do.
standing.why_now: Runs twice a week year-round and is one of the few genuinely free weeknight drop-in activities.

standing.title: Whitney Museum free Friday evening
standing.description: The Whitney is free to all every Friday evening from 5 to 10pm, and also on the second Sunday of each month.
standing.time_note: Free admission Fridays 5-10pm. Free tickets are limited and released in advance.
standing.practical_note: Reserve the free timed ticket ahead; walk-up availability runs out on busy evenings.
standing.date_idea_reason: Free evening museum hours next to the High Line and a dense stretch of bars, so the museum is the anchor rather than the whole plan.
standing.why_now: A standing free window that makes a good anchor for a Friday evening in the Meatpacking District.

standing.title: Queens Night Market
standing.address: Behind the New York Hall of Science, 47-01 111th St, Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Queens, NY 11368
standing.description: Open-air night market behind the New York Hall of Science with about a hundred independent food, art, and merchandise vendors, deliberately kept low-priced.
standing.time_note: Saturdays 4pm to midnight. Note the seasonal gap between late August and mid September.
standing.practical_note: Outdoors and cash-friendly; the adjacent lot charges for parking, so the 7 train is easier.

price.display: Free entry; most dishes capped at a few dollars

standing.date_idea_reason: Cheap, walkable, and genuinely varied: dozens of cuisines in one loop, good for a low-pressure evening.
standing.why_now: Runs every Saturday evening in season; the 7 train to 111th St drops you four blocks away.

standing.title: MoMA free Friday evening
standing.description: MoMA offers free admission on Friday evenings. Free tickets are limited, released in advance, and go quickly.
standing.time_note: Free Friday evenings, roughly 4-8pm. Confirm the current window and ticket release on moma.org.
standing.practical_note: Book the free timed ticket the moment it is released; the line for walk-ups is long.
standing.why_now: A standing weekly free window at a museum that is otherwise one of the most expensive in the city.

holiday_plan.intro: For Oct. 10-12, prioritize timed-entry art sites and rail-friendly Hudson Valley trips, and treat Oct. 12 as a holiday operating exception to verify rather than assumed extra time off. Several strong picks are car-free, but holiday-weekend traffic can make driving estimates unreliable, so check schedules and ticket windows before committing.

trips.title: Car-free Beacon art day: Dia Beacon plus riverfront
trips.why: Dia Beacon is open Friday-Monday 10 AM-5 PM seasonally, making Monday Oct. 12 workable; Oct. 10 also has Dia's Isang Yun: Images concert at 2 PM, free with museum admission but with limited seating and separate registration.
trips.transport: Car-free: Metro-North Hudson Line to Beacon, then walk or short local taxi/rideshare to Dia; driving is possible but Dia notes on-site parking is limited and additional parking may be at Beacon station on busy weekends/holidays.
trips.time_budget: Comfortable full day from NYC; Dia's own driving directions cite about 80 minutes from NYC in normal conditions, while rail time must be checked in the MTA schedule tool.
trips.booking_note: Dia says advance reservations are suggested but not required; tickets for the next month become available on the 15th of the current month. Register separately for the Oct. 10 concert if choosing that date.

trips.title: Car-free Cold Spring / Hudson Highlands hike and village day
trips.destination: Cold Spring and Hudson Highlands State Park Preserve, NY
trips.why: Best for a low-cost outdoors day: the official park page notes more than 70 miles of trails, scenery from easy to challenging terrain, and sunrise-to-sunset park hours. It is practical by Metro-North, with Little Stony Point parking at the Cold Spring train station noted by NY State Parks.
trips.transport: Car-free: Metro-North Hudson Line to Cold Spring. Car-required only if combining multiple trailheads or nearby towns; official park page warns parking is limited and illegal parking may be ticketed/towed.
trips.time_budget: Full day; start early because the park is open sunrise to sunset and official guidance stresses leaving enough time to complete hikes.
trips.booking_note: No park ticket noted for ordinary hiking, but use official NYS Parks maps, stay on marked trails, bring water, and do not rely on third-party trail descriptions. Overnight camping and fire are prohibited.

trips.title: Hudson + Olana art-landscape overnight
trips.destination: Hudson and Olana State Historic Site, NY
trips.why: A one-night escape pairs Hudson's food/antiques scene with Olana's 250-acre designed landscape. Olana's official page says the landscape is free and open daily 8 AM-sunset, and tours are open Monday Oct. 12 even though regular tour hours are Tuesday-Sunday in season.
trips.transport: Car-free-ish: Amtrak to Hudson, then taxi/rideshare to Olana; car helpful for flexibility between Hudson, Olana, and nearby villages. Official Amtrak pages were blocked during research, so schedules remain unconfirmed from source.
trips.time_budget: Best as one night rather than a rushed day, because Olana tour timing, Hudson meals, and local transfers need slack.
trips.booking_note: Olana says tours sell out quickly and advance reservations are strongly recommended; historic house access is by ticket only. Arrive 30 minutes before a scheduled tour and leave 30 minutes between multiple tours.

trips.title: Storm King Art Center by bus package or car
trips.why: Large-scale outdoor sculpture is a strong fall art-and-nature day without stretching beyond the region. Storm King lists public hours Wednesday-Monday 10 AM-6 PM, closed Tuesdays, with final entry at 5 PM; Coach USA lists a NYC package operating through Nov. 29, 2026 on days including Sunday and Monday.
trips.transport: Car-free option: Coach USA/ShortLine round trip from Port Authority with museum admission included. Car-required alternative: drive/rideshare to 20 Old Pleasant Hill Rd.; no overnight parking. Train-only is not direct: Storm King says Beacon is about 30 minutes away by car and Salisbury Mills-Cornwall about 10 minutes by car.
trips.time_budget: Full day; Coach USA itinerary shown as 10:30 AM NYC departure, 11:40 AM arrival, 4 PM Storm King departure, 5:15 PM NYC arrival.
trips.booking_note: Use the Coach USA package if going car-free; admission is not included with Metro-North/NJ Transit rail. Verify the specific Oct. 10-12 date before purchase and check any weather/air-quality changes affecting bike rentals or outdoor amenities.

trips.title: Great Jack O'Lantern Blaze evening in Croton-on-Hudson
trips.why: Distinctive seasonal event close to NYC: the official Blaze site lists 2026 event dates Sept. 18-Nov. 8, timed admission only, with more than 7,000 pumpkins at Van Cortlandt Manor. It works as an evening add-on to a lower-Hudson day.
trips.transport: Car-free-ish: Metro-North Hudson Line to Croton-Harmon, then confirm the safest walking/local transfer plan to Van Cortlandt Manor before booking. Car-required if you want maximum schedule control; official page says parking is free, but do not assume entry without a timed ticket.
trips.time_budget: Evening-focused half day; pair with Tarrytown/Sleepy Hollow or a daytime Hudson Line stop if train schedules line up.
